title: Paridyum Product Registry
description: The complete set of products Paridyum sells, the lifecycle they move through, and what each owes at each stage. Declared under ADR-0050. A product is a FOURTH governance axis, orthogonal to `scope` (repository class) and `applies_to` (repository name): one product spans several repositories and one repository serves several products, so a product could never have been a scope value. C-0008 decides membership — if tenant traffic can reach it, it is a product — and `kind` decides what evidence it owes. This file does not list repositories; a repository declares its product in manifest.yaml and the mapping is read in that direction only, because a fact has one home (RFC-0015) and cross-repo views are generated rather than hand-authored (ADR-0040).

version.description: Registry format version. Bump only for a breaking shape change, which needs an ADR.

stages.description: The lifecycle, in order. Ordering is semantic: `product.sequencing_respects_second_vertical_rule` reads the position of a product's stage in this list, so reordering entries changes what the gate enforces and is a decision, not a tidy-up.

stage.description: Machine-readable stage id, locale-independent per ADR-0032.

dossier.description: What each kind owes at each stage, cumulatively. THE TAXONOMY LIVES HERE RATHER THAN IN THE TYPE SYSTEM: adding a required document kind is one entry in this array, not a directory, a prefix, a schema enum value and five hardcoded sites. That is the same trade ADR-0022 made for artifact types and ADR-0014 made for check ids, applied to the one list a growing company extends most often.

artifacts.description: Artifact-type PREFIXES from artifact-registry.yaml that a product of this kind must carry, naming it in `product:`, by this stage. An unknown prefix is a hard failure for the reason an unknown check id is (ADR-0014): a dossier requirement nothing can resolve is a requirement nothing enforces.

slots.description: Things owed that have NO artifact type yet, deliberately. A slot is a named obligation whose first instance does not exist — declaring the type now would produce the empty-directory state `glossary/` was in for the life of the repository, where unvalidated prose sat in a repository whose founding argument is that unenforced prose is a suggestion. A slot becomes a type the day something real has to go in it.

products.description: One entry per product, sorted by `product`. MAY BE EMPTY OF ANY GIVEN KIND, and the absence of catalogue products is currently load-bearing: registering a vertical before its selecting evidence exists is what C-0006 anti-goal 6 forbids, and a registry that made it cheap would be the mechanism for the drift it was written to prevent. Uniqueness of `product` is enforced by the gate, not expressible here.

product.description: The slug. Immutable and never reused, for the reason an artifact id is: it is the permanent handle for this product in frontmatter, manifests and git history. Locale-independent per ADR-0032 — this is a machine identifier and the display name is `name`.

name.description: The human-readable name. May change; the slug may not.

kind.description: Decides which dossier binds. `platform` is Paridyum itself, whose market evidence is the org-level artifacts. `capability` is a runtime capability a tenant can buy (C-0008), which owes a tenant-facing interface rather than market research. `catalogue` is a vertical Paridyum operates and franchises (BET-0004, BET-0005), and is the only kind C-0006's evidence obligation binds.
